00254.mechanism: Non-steroidal inhibition of aromatase lowers oestrogen production.
00254.schedule: Anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily continuously; no planned cycle break.
00254.daily_practical_instructions: 1 mg once daily, with or without food; swallow whole. Skip a missed dose and take the next scheduled daily dose. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not repeat it.
00254.treatment_duration: The consultant specifies duration according to indication, prior endocrine treatment, response and tolerability. Do not convert the general advanced-disease until-progression wording into an indefinite adjuvant course.
00254.menopause_boundary: Confirmed postmenopausal endocrine state is required for this monotherapy pathway. A separate ovarian-suppression combination must be prescribed and monitored explicitly; chemotherapy-related amenorrhoea alone is not a documented suppression plan.

no_universal_schedule: No infusion visit, pump connection or pump removal for the oral medicine itself.

No routine echo, ECG, CT or tumour-marker interval is specified by these AI monotherapy sources; additional therapies and disease setting may have their own requirements.

body_map_focus.message: Aching or stiffness can affect activity; tell the team if it is limiting so supportive measures or an alternative can be considered.
Hot flushes and sweating may disturb sleep; practical symptom support can help.
Dryness and discomfort can occur; ask about suitable treatments before using hormone-containing products.
Bone thinning can develop over time without symptoms; the bone-health and DXA plan is important.

00254.timeline_notes: Use a continuous-treatment horizon (starting / first months / ongoing years) rather than a day-of-cycle toxicity curve with predictable nadir/recovery. Side-effect timing varies; no fixed date input is needed.
00254.supportive_care: Minimal emetic risk; no routine prophylactic antiemetic, steroid premedication or G-CSF for AI monotherapy. NCCP recommends calcium/vitamin D and weight-bearing exercise; the team individualises supplementation and bone-protective medication.

source_differences.detail: NCCP broad HR-positive indications coexist with an additional eligibility bullet listing tamoxifen contraindication or intolerance. An explicit report that tamoxifen is suitable produces a review message; missing history does not block unrelated partial assessment.

NCCP p2 says severe hepatic impairment is not recommended; NCCP p1 and the linked SmPC §§4.2/4.4 describe moderate/severe hepatic caution. The card follows the stricter NCCP no-treatment recommendation pending specialist review and does not mislabel severe hepatic disease as an absolute SmPC contraindication. Child–Pugh A/B/C is the UI classification of mild/moderate/severe impairment.

The linked Teva anastrozole SmPC lists advanced disease, whereas NCCP also lists adjuvant indications. The linked Aromasin SmPC describes switching after 2–3 years of tamoxifen and completing 5 total years, whereas NCCP also has broader adjuvant/extended-adjuvant entries. Preserve NCCP indication codes; verify the actual dispensed product and individual endocrine-duration plan rather than silently substituting product wording.

NCCP says risk-based baseline and regular/as-clinically-indicated BMD, without a single fixed repeat interval. Any proposed 1–2-year DXA schedule must be separately cited to a guideline and individualised, not presented as an exact NCCP mandate.

00254.additional_safety: Persistent vaginal bleeding or new tendon pain/swelling should be assessed. Clarify the NCCP additional eligibility wording about tamoxifen contraindication/intolerance with the consultant.

00371.schedule: Letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily continuously; no planned cycle break.
00371.daily_practical_instructions: 2.5 mg once daily, with or without food; swallow whole. Take a missed dose when remembered unless the next dose is within 2–3 hours; then skip it. source_differences.detail: NCCP p2 supplies 2.5 mg every other day in Child–Pugh C. The NCCP-linked 2019 HPRA SmPC describes insufficient data/close supervision but does not prescribe that frequency reduction. The explicit NCCP instruction is displayed with this distinction and consultant/pharmacy confirmation.

NCCP no-adjustment/dialysis-expected-no-adjustment wording is broader than the linked SmPC, which says evidence is insufficient below CrCl 10 mL/min. Low CrCl/dialysis remains a specialist review; no reduced dose is guessed.

neoadjuvant_mapping.sequence: Daily letrozole → tumour response review during 4–8 months → breast surgery or alternative treatment discussion
neoadjuvant_mapping.detail: NCCP allows 4–8 months to optimise tumour reduction. Inadequate response requires reviewing/discontinuing the neoadjuvant course and planning surgery and/or alternatives; do not automatically extend.
